title: Chapters 6–9 — check what stuck
intro: Nine self-check questions across the calculus chapters. My own checks against the lessons, not an official paper.

questions.prompt: A sphere inflates at a constant volume rate Q. What happens to dr/dt as it grows?
choices: It stays constant, since Q is constant
It falls, as Q/(4πr²) — the same inflow spread over an ever-larger surface, so radius goes as t^(1/3)
It rises, because the sphere has more surface to expand into
It oscillates with the radius
questions.explanation: Differentiate the relation, not the quantity: V = (4/3)πr³ gives dV/dt = 4πr²·dr/dt. Volume is linear in time; radius is not.

questions.prompt: f′(c) = 0 and f″(c) = 0. What can you conclude?
choices: It is an inflection point
It is a minimum
Nothing yet — the second-derivative test is inconclusive, so fall back to the first-derivative test and read the sign change
It is a maximum
questions.explanation: f″(c) = 0 is genuinely inconclusive. It may be a max, a min, or an inflection; only the sign change of f′ across c distinguishes them.

questions.prompt: On [-2, 6], x³ - 3x² - 9x + 15 has a local maximum of 20 at x = -1. What is its absolute maximum?
choices: 20, at the local maximum
69, at the endpoint x = 6 — where f′(6) = 27 and the curve is still climbing when the interval runs out
-12, at the local minimum
It has no absolute maximum on a closed interval
questions.explanation: Absolute extrema on [a, b] must compare the interior critical points against the endpoints. A search that only solves f′ = 0 cannot find this one.

questions.prompt: What does the + C in an indefinite integral physically represent in an inertial navigator?
choices: Accumulated numerical error
The sensor's bias
The initial velocity — assume it is zero while the vehicle is already moving and position drifts linearly forever
Nothing; it cancels out in practice
questions.explanation: Differentiation destroys the constant. Integration recovers the shape but not the offset, and a default of zero is a claim that the system started at rest.

questions.prompt: Why does ILATE say to take u = ln x when integrating ∫ln x dx?
choices: Because logarithms are always harder
Because Logarithmic outranks Algebraic, leaving ∫v du easier than the original — it resolves to x·ln x - x + C
Because dv must always be the whole integrand
Because ln x has no derivative
questions.explanation: The whole skill in parts is choosing u so the REMAINING integral is simpler. Choosing the other way round here makes it worse.

questions.prompt: On symmetric bounds [-a, a], what does an odd integrand give you?
choices: Twice the integral from 0 to a
Exactly zero, with no computation at all
The same as an even integrand
An undefined result
questions.explanation: Odd cancels exactly; even gives 2∫₀ᵃ. It is an O(1) check in front of an O(N) computation — which is why roll moment vanishes across a symmetric wing while lift accumulates.

questions.prompt: The trapezoid error on a smooth integrand goes 0.107, 0.027, 0.0067 at N = 10, 20, 40. What does that tell you?
choices: The method is diverging
Error falls as roughly 1/N² — it quarters each time N doubles, which is why doubling resolution is the meaningful move
Error falls linearly with N
Round-off dominates already
questions.explanation: Quartering per doubling is the 1/N² signature. Adding a few slices achieves little; doubling achieves a factor of four.

questions.prompt: After substituting u = g(x) in a DEFINITE integral and translating the limits, what should you do?
choices: Back-substitute to x, then apply the original limits
Evaluate between the translated limits and stop — back-substituting and reapplying the old limits corrects the same thing twice
Always double the result
Re-derive du from scratch
questions.explanation: Translating the limits is what makes the substitution definite. Back-substitution belongs to indefinite integrals, where there are no limits to carry.

questions.prompt: What is the degree of y′ + cos(y′) = 0?
choices: Undefined — the equation is not polynomial in its derivatives, so the concept does not apply
questions.explanation: Degree requires the equation to be polynomial in its derivatives. 'Undefined' is the correct and informative answer; inventing a number there sends you toward a method that cannot work.
